anomalies.observed: On the 'MAIN PUMP & VALVE DRIVERS' sheet (page 1 bottom / page 3 right) the ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch is T6, an AO3400A (30 V small-signal N-MOSFET), while the AON6407 (T7) has been placed instead as the 24 V reverse-polarity protection FET on the input rail (page 1, 'Reverse polarity protection').
anomalies.expected: The specification's component table assigns the valve to the AON6407: 'T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch'. A 24 V inductive load switched with a 30 V part (only clamped to +24 V by D2 SS34) leaves essentially no margin for flyback/ringing.

evidence.quote: T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch | Netlist: drives ATO_VALVE net; gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904).
Page 3 (sheet 1/1, row F, col ~3): ATO Valve switch transistor labelled 'T6 AO3400A'; page 1 row A: reverse-polarity FET labelled 'T7 AON6407'.

anomalies.impact: The valve MOSFET is rated far below the design intent; repeated inductive switching of the 24 V solenoid can push the 30 V part into avalanche and cause premature failure of the ATO valve driver.

anomalies.observed: On the 'WATER LEVEL SENSOR/SWITCHES' sheet the LiDAR module PR4 is fully wired: VCC to +5V and SDA/SCL through header H6 to NET0014/NET0020, which are the ESP32 I2C_SDA/I2C_SCL nets (see SoC sheet, IO4/IO5).
anomalies.expected: The specification states the LiDAR is not connected in this design: 'its pins are "free" and it is marked on_board: no / excluded from the board; it is not wired into any net', and water level is sensed by an ultrasonic transducer on two GPIOs, not by an I2C LiDAR.

evidence.quote: the r2 netlist shows PR1 with on_board: no, in_bom: yes, and all four pins (VCC, SDA, SCL, GND) typed free — i.e., it is not connected to any net in this design.
Page 1 row D: 'PR4 LiDAR' pins VCC/SDA/SCL/GND/TX tied to H6 PB_L_25mm; H6 pins 2/3 carry NET0014 and NET0020 (the I2C_SDA/I2C_SCL nets).

anomalies.impact: The board presents an unaccounted I2C device on the main bus and provides no working ultrasonic level interface; an ultrasonic sensor plugged into H6 would short trigger/echo onto the I2C lines, and the firmware (which has no LiDAR block) gets no valid distance reading.

anomalies.observed: The global label NET0098 appears both on the TPS62933 feedback divider node (U6 pin 8 / R9–R51 junction, '24V-5V 3A BUCK' block) and on ESP32-C6 pin IO2 (SoC block). The same net name also reappears on the EC isolator sheet.
anomalies.expected: The buck feedback node is a dedicated analog sense net (spec calls it /0V8_BK) and must not be tied to an MCU pin; per the spec pin map IO2 is the ATO_VALVE drive ('ATO_VALVE | IO2').

evidence.quote: feedback via R13/R14/R15 ... as named by the /BST_BK, /RT_BK, /SS_BK, /0V8_BK nets
Page 1 row A: buck FB pin labelled NET0098 at the R9/R51 node; page 1 row B SoC: IO2/SPI_MISO pin labelled NET0098.

anomalies.impact: If genuine, the 5 V regulator's 0.8 V sense node is shorted to an MCU pin (and possibly an isolator signal), corrupting 5 V regulation and clashing with the firmware's use of that GPIO.

parsed.summary: The drawing deviates from the specification in at least two readable ways: the ATO valve is switched by an AO3400A instead of the specified AON6407 (a 30 V part on a 24 V inductive load), and the LiDAR that the spec states is unwired is in fact connected onto the I2C bus; a third, less certain net-name collision (NET0098) appears to tie the buck feedback node to ESP32 IO2.
